messages:
Sam: Heads up — saw a sharp tail-latency spike on eu-west dedicated around 02:15 UTC. GPU PCIe utilization jumped and a single tenant's DMA bursts looked correlated with inference p99 increases. attaching quick notes.

Jordan: Which pool / slice? any tenant id?

Sam: pool: euw-dedicated-3, slice: slot-42. tenant id T-phi. logs below: 
```
[02:14:58] gpu0 pci_dma: util 96% burst_len=1.2ms repeat=5
[02:15:01] infer_latency p50=18ms p95=123ms p99=420ms
[02:15:02] nvlink_err: transient backpressure
```
Not full OOM but PCIe saturation/egress coupling for neighboring slots.

Maya: Ugh, we've seen a similar pattern in apac last month. Suggestion: implement a "noise-aware" routing policy that steers variable-size requests away from shared slices when we detect repeated short DMA bursts. Basically: detect burst signature -> mark tenant as noisy -> route to either: dedicated reserved slice or quantized/sharded model variant.

Ben: That helps reliability but increases cost if we move tenants to reserved slices. Can we do a softer approach first? e.g., apply egress policing + reclaim small KV-cache budget + temporary soft-eviction (slower teardown backoff) so noisy tenant gets rate-limited before we reassign.

Asha: Soft-eviction is promising. Flow I'd propose:
1) detection window: 30s of >80% PCIe util with >3 microbursts
2) automated mitigation: apply egress policer (burst=200MB/s, sustained=50MB/s) + reduce CPU-side prefetch threads for that tenant
3) concurrent routing: if mitigation doesn't reduce p99 in 60s, shift to reserved or quantized fallback variant

Jordan: How reliable is detection? False positives could throttle legit spikes (batch jobs). We need tenant labels: is this interactive traffic? T-phi is mostly low-latency interactive.

Sam: detection will use combined signals: pci_dma rate, io_wait, nvlink errs, and tail-latency. threshold needs to be conservative. I can prototype a rule in 1h.

Maya: Also add a warm-pool prefetch: for tenants we might temporarily promote, provision a 1-2 GPU warm slice so migration is fast and avoid cold-start pressure. That keeps latency steady but costs are short-lived.

Ben: Cost model: warm-slice for 2 mins per noisy event x events/week x number of tenants. We should simulate. I'll run a quick cost estimate if Sam posts event histogram.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2024-6372 linked to thread. Auto-tags: pci-bus, noisy-neighbor, eu-west.

Sam: Quick dump of recent event histogram (last 7 days):
```
T-phi: 12 events >30s
Other noisy-ids: 5, 2, 1
Peak window: 02:00-03:30 UTC (lower traffic for others)
```
So it's mostly T-phi recurring.

Asha: Action items:
- Sam: prototype detection rule + a reversible egress policer runbook (by EOD)
- Ben: run the warm-slice cost sim and a pricing suggestion for customer-aware shielding (by tomorrow)
- Maya: sketch routing fallback flows + model-variant tagging to enable automatic quantized swap (by EOD)
- Ops: enable temporary canary of soft-eviction on euw-dedicated-3 next maintenance window

Jordan: +1. Also add a metric: "noise-shielded-tenants" so product can see how often we do this and decide if we should sell it as a feature.

Sam: I'll start the prototype now and post a short PR with the detection rule. If anyone wants access to the traces, ping me. :eyes:

Maya: ping me on PR review, I can help wire the routing rule to the router service. :+1:

Ben: I'll queue the cost sim. If warm-slice overhead is >10% of committed pool cost we should default to egress-police + quantized fallback instead.

ops-bot: Scheduled canary: soft-eviction on euw-dedicated-3 at 2024-07-29T03:00:00Z (maintenance window).

Sam: Thanks. keeping this thread as the coordination log.
